dataset.name: Ego2Web
dataset.license_or_access_note: Existing research authorization confirmed by project owner; no public release performed.

original_annotations: The existing Ego2Web prompt asks for flour-sack wording at 130–140 seconds. This is an index to a bakery recording, not evidence for the new kneading task.

observed_events.description: The wearer weighs and handles a pale cohesive dough mass in a white plastic bucket beside a scale, then pulls a portion from the mass by hand. The mixer head and kneading attachment are not exposed in the selected V0 packet.
The wearer carries the same dough bucket to the floor-standing mixer, tips dough into the steel mixing bowl and removes the bucket; the kneading attachment and bowl contents become visible.
The wearer pours a clear liquid from a measuring jug into the mixer bowl; a kneading attachment and its movement through the pale dough/flour mixture are visible.
The wearer closes the metal wire bowl guard and reaches to the machine controls.

supported_claims.text: The V0 packet shows portioning/preparation in a bucket, not the kind of kneading attachment or machine operation used for the batch. Hand handling does not establish that all kneading will be manual.
The V1 packet reveals the same dough bucket being emptied into the machine and a moving kneading attachment in a steel bowl, followed by the protective guard and controls.
The later setup is part of preparing the same batch, not an independent tool switched in response to a new user instruction.

Later released views expose a deep steel bowl, a curved overhead kneading element beside a vertical bar, a front control panel and a large movable wire cover. They support the general operating arrangement, not a required brand/model or an inferred safety interlock.

source_inspection.v0_visibility_check: All V0 frames preserve full 640x360 source frames, with no spatial crops or overlays. Bucket, scale and bakery background are visible; none shows the mixer head or its kneading attachment. A rack/edge appliance surface alone does not identify the required method.

original_recipe_request_shortcut.finding: Sally ICkHBCcRX74 teaches hand kneading and motor-driven dough-hook kneading. A general kneading request has a no-scene universal answer over the viable hand/mixer setups in that captured window. Keep the lesson; do not remove it to manufacture visual necessity.
original_recipe_request_shortcut.superseded_instruction: Save a beginner tutorial for mixing and kneading dough with the kind of setup I'm using here.

setup_operation_feasibility.revised_useful_purpose: Learn operation of the actual dough-mixing equipment rather than any interchangeable method for making dough. No requirement to copy brand, recipe or commercial scale.
setup_operation_feasibility.source_structure: V1 shows a deep steel bowl, fixed vertical bar beside a curved overhead kneading element, a front control panel, and a large movable wire cover over the bowl. V0 has none of the mixing-head/attachment or control-panel evidence.
setup_operation_feasibility.scope_counterexample: At about 0s the original 180s clip briefly exposes a large mixer body. The proposed session starts with the later continuous 36–55s weighing and portioning stage, rather than claiming the full source hides machinery. No spatial crop is applied. Reviewer must assess whether this is a natural session start.

bounded_repair_check.observed: The wearer handles dough and moves a padded chair at 0–7s. At 5–6s the same olive-green machine head, two front round controls/green buttons and large steel bowl are visible. At 14–36s the wearer weighs and portions dough in buckets. No earlier distinct operating machine/category or later corrective change is established.
bounded_repair_check.conclusion: No valid replacement relation. Stop this source; retain its authentic search windows, candidate judgments, public metadata, released frames, provenance and independent review history.

construct.research_question: Can later evidence of the operating equipment correct an initially broad machine-training selection without discarding an already applicable general operation guide?
construct.belief_before: The wearer prepares and portions dough in a bucket. No mixing head, kneading attachment or control panel is exposed in the released initial packet; the kind of dough-mixing machine is not established.
construct.belief_after: The same batch enters a deep steel bowl under a fixed machine head; the curved kneading element, adjacent vertical bar, front controls and movable wire cover establish the machine operating arrangement.
construct.required_behavior_change: Replace a lesson for a different operating arrangement if initially saved; keep a guide already teaching the revealed equipment. Save one useful operation lesson, not an extra recipe.
construct.no_update_failure: A hand-mixer, breadmaker, bottom-drive or planetary attachment/setup lesson remains despite the later reveal of a different machine arrangement.
construct.overupdate_failure: Discard a useful tabletop or multi-equipment spiral/bowl-mixer demonstration solely for different brand, capacity, recipe or control labels.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: The text requests operating the equipment without naming its mechanical arrangement. The real complete window has several distinct operator workflows. Later source frames identify the guarded bowl and curved-kneader/bar system; the useful equipment class comes from the scene.

task_blueprint.instruction: Save a beginner tutorial for operating the kind of dough-mixing machine I'm using here.

observed.why: The bowl view exposes the curved overhead kneader beside a fixed vertical bar; V1:3 exposes the hinged wire bowl cover. The source no longer supports a different machine assembly/operation guide.

catalog_resolution.answer_boundary_rule: The request is equipment-operation learning, not a recipe or generic way to develop gluten. Initially the equipment category is unresolved. Finally accept practical operation instruction for the revealed guarded steel-bowl machine with an overhead curved kneading element and adjacent fixed bar, including useful general or multi-equipment demonstrations. Machine size, brand, recipe and exact control layout are not requirements. Do not require a particular safety interlock or a complete industrial certification course. Planetary attachment assembly, bottom-driven dough makers, hand mixers, breadmakers and roller machines have different operator workflows. Demonstrations can qualify when they actually show operation; product images or purchase comparisons alone do not.

tasks.rejection_reason: V0 (40–55s) shows only dough in a bucket and hand portioning, with no identified machine being operated. V1 first identifies the machine and therefore cannot invalidate a source-established earlier equipment category. The one bounded repair inspection of the natural early 0–36s interval found the same olive-green fixed-head steel-bowl mixer at 5–6s, not a different earlier machine or a misleading configuration corrected later. Including that real context yields the same applicable equipment class before and after; excluding it yields first recognition, not replacement.
